## TL;DR

Diff syntax highlighting now runs Shiki with only the active palette pair (GitHub light/dark or Catppuccin Latte/Mocha): themes load on first use per family, `highlightPair` takes `themeFamily`, and results are cached per content hash and family. `DiffView` passes the family from `useConfigStore().uiTheme` via `diffHighlightFamilyForUiTheme`, so changing design theme re-highlights; light/dark still swaps via CSS only. Tests cover mapping, Catppuccin variable names, cache/metrics behavior, and a logged bench on `src/core/db.ts`.

## Work and rationale

The diff highlighter used `codeToTokensWithThemes` with four Shiki themes at once so tokens carried GitHub and Catppuccin colours on every span and CSS could switch without re-tokenizing light/dark. That paid four colour passes per highlight call even though only one family matches the current `[data-ui-theme]`.

The fix keeps the same CSS contract (`--shiki-light` / `--shiki-dark` vs `--shiki-catppuccin-light` / `--shiki-catppuccin-dark`) and the same selectors in `style.css`. The highlighter now chooses a `DiffHighlightThemeFamily`: `github` for every UI theme except `catppuccin`, which maps to the Catppuccin Shiki pair. `createHighlighterCore` starts with no themes; `ensureThemesForFamily` calls `core.loadTheme` with dynamic imports for exactly that family’s two theme modules, once per process.

`highlightPair` requires `themeFamily` and passes only the corresponding two-theme object to Shiki, so each pane does two passes instead of four. A stable cache key hashes filename plus joined before/after lines with FNV-1a, keyed by family, so switching away and back reuses stored HTML without calling Shiki again. Metrics `shikiTokenizeRuns` and `cacheHits` support tests.

`DiffView` watches `diffHighlightFamily` (derived from config store `uiTheme`) together with file contents, so toggling Catppuccin in the sidebar while a diff is open triggers a new highlight with the right variables.

Vitest resets cache and metrics in `beforeEach`/`afterEach` to avoid order dependence. A benchmark test reads `db.ts` and logs wall time for PR notes, but is **skipped unless** `REPOOS_SYNTAX_HIGHLIGHT_BENCH=1` so server `repoos check` stays within deadlines (full-file highlight can take many seconds on shared runners).

## Approaches tried

Lazy theme loading via `loadTheme` on the shared `HighlighterCore` kept one engine instance and avoided loading all four theme chunks up front. Alternative of two separate highlighter instances would duplicate grammar state and was rejected.

Cache stores full `HighlightPairResult` objects; hashing content avoids holding duplicate strings in the key. Plain-text paths skip the cache as before.

## Challenges and blockers

Shiki’s variant keys for the Catppuccin pair (`catppuccinLight` / `catppuccinDark`) differ from GitHub’s (`light` / `dark`); tests assert Catppuccin output uses the catppuccin CSS variables and not `--shiki-light`. Formatter required `bun run fmt` after edits.

## Key learnings

`HighlighterCore` accepts empty `themes: []` at construction and loads themes later with `loadTheme`, which matches the goal of family-scoped dynamic chunks. Wiring the diff view to the config store’s `uiTheme` is enough to get `data-ui-theme` changes without reading the DOM. For PR timing, the checked-in vitest bench is a reproducible anchor even though absolute milliseconds vary by CPU load.
